content.raw_text: 我亲爱的孩子，你今天一天都在让我讲关于孙悟空，那个美猴王的故事。我一直在告诉你要等到睡觉以前我才会讲他的故事。那么现在是睡觉的时候了，所以我现在要告诉你猴王在天上人间找麻烦的另一个故事。今晚我会给你讲他和桃子的故事！

sentences.text: 我亲爱的孩子，你今天一天都在让我讲关于孙悟空，那个美猴王的故事。
sentences.translation: My dear child, you have been asking me to tell the story of Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, all day today.
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces the topic of telling a story about Sun Wukong, a famous character in Chinese mythology. The structure '一天都' emphasizes that the action of asking to hear the story has been happening throughout the entire day.

sentences.text: 我一直在告诉你要等到睡觉以前我才会讲他的故事。
sentences.translation: I have been telling you that I will only tell his story before going to sleep.
sentences.explanation: The structure '要...才...' indicates that something will only happen under certain conditions. In this case, the speaker will only tell the story before going to sleep.

sentences.text: 那么现在是睡觉的时候了，所以我现在要告诉你猴王在天上人间找麻烦的另一个故事。
sentences.translation: So now it's time to sleep, so I'm going to tell you another story about the Monkey King causing trouble in heaven and on earth.
sentences.explanation: This sentence contains a complex structure with multiple clauses and particles. The use of '了' indicates a change of situation, and '所以' is used to connect the reason for the action. The phrase '猴王在天上人间' is a set phrase referring to the Monkey King causing trouble in both heaven and on earth.

words.definition: particle indicating completion or change of situation

sentences.text: 今晚我会给你讲他和桃子的故事！
sentences.translation: Tonight I will tell you the story of him and Peach!
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure follows the pattern of subject + verb + object. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate possession or relationship between 'him' and 'Peach'.

content.raw_text: 我已经告诉过你，这个猴王是出生在奥莱国 花果山上的一只小石猴。因为他发现了水帘洞的秘密才成了猴王。这以后，花果山上的所有猴子都住在水帘洞里，安全快乐。但是猴王想要一直活着，所以他去了很远的地方，跟一位大师学习，大师给了他一个名字叫孙悟空。他学到了长生不死的秘密，还学到了怎么用筋斗云走得又快又远。他还有一个武器：金箍棒。他可以把它变得很大，也可以把它变得非常小放在他的耳朵里。

sentences.text: 我已经告诉过你，这个猴王是出生在奥莱国 花果山上的一只小石猴。
sentences.translation: I have already told you, this Monkey King was born on the Flower Fruit Mountain in the Orléans country.
sentences.explanation: The structure '告诉过' indicates that the action of telling has been completed in the past. The use of '一只' before '小石猴' is a measure word indicating 'one' for animals.

sentences.text: 因为他发现了水帘洞的秘密才成了猴王。
sentences.translation: Because he discovered the secret of the Water Curtain Cave, he became the Monkey King.
sentences.explanation: The structure '因为...才...' is used to indicate a cause and effect relationship, where the second action happens unexpectedly as a result of the first action.

sentences.text: 这以后，花果山上的所有猴子都住在水帘洞里，安全快乐。
sentences.translation: After that, all the monkeys on Flower Fruit Mountain lived in Water Curtain Cave, safe and happy.
sentences.explanation: The structure '都...在...' is used to indicate that all the monkeys are living inside the Water Curtain Cave.

sentences.text: 但是猴王想要一直活着，所以他去了很远的地方，跟一位大师学习，大师给了他一个名字叫孙悟空。
sentences.translation: But the Monkey King wanted to live forever, so he went to a faraway place to learn from a master, who gave him a name called Sun Wukong.
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces the Monkey King's desire to live forever and his journey to learn from a master, who gives him the name Sun Wukong.

sentences.text: 他学到了长生不死的秘密，还学到了怎么用筋斗云走得又快又远。
sentences.translation: He learned the secret of immortality, and also learned how to use the somersault cloud to travel fast and far.
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces the concept of immortality and the ability to use a mythical cloud for fast and far travel, which are common themes in Chinese mythology and literature.

sentences.text: 他还有一个武器：金箍棒。
sentences.translation: He also has a weapon: the golden hoop rod.
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces a new weapon, the 'golden hoop rod', that the character possesses.

sentences.text: 他可以把它变得很大，也可以把它变得非常小放在他的耳朵里。
sentences.translation: He can make it very big, or he can make it very small and put it in his ear.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the structure of using '把' before an object to indicate the object of an action in Chinese grammar. It also demonstrates the use of '很' (very) and '非常' (very) to emphasize the degree of an adjective.

words.definition: used before an object to indicate the object of an action
used before an object to indicate the object of an action

content.raw_text: 孙悟空是一只非常强大的猴子，天上的玉皇大帝很不想他去找麻烦,所以请孙悟空住在天宫里，叫他齐天大圣。但孙悟空没事做。所以他认识了很多朋友，吃了很多好吃的东西，去了天宫里的每一个地方，很快乐地生活着。

sentences.text: 孙悟空是一只非常强大的猴子，天上的玉皇大帝很不想他去找麻烦，所以请孙悟空住在天宫里，叫他齐天大圣。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong is a very powerful monkey. The Jade Emperor in heaven really doesn't want him to cause trouble, so he asks Sun Wukong to live in the Heavenly Palace and names him the Great Sage Equal to Heaven.
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces the character Sun Wukong, a powerful monkey, and explains how the Jade Emperor asks him to live in the Heavenly Palace to prevent trouble. The title 'Great Sage Equal to Heaven' is given to Sun Wukong.

sentences.text: 但孙悟空没事做。
sentences.translation: But Sun Wukong has nothing to do.
sentences.explanation: The structure '没事做' means 'nothing to do' in this context. It is a common phrase to indicate having free time or being idle.

sentences.text: 所以他认识了很多朋友，吃了很多好吃的东西，去了天宫里的每一个地方，很快乐地生活着。
sentences.translation: So he made a lot of friends, ate a lot of delicious food, visited every place in the heavenly palace, and lived happily.
sentences.explanation: The structure 'verb + 了 + description' indicates completion of an action. The particle '着' is used to indicate an ongoing action in this sentence.

content.raw_text: 玉皇大帝很担心孙悟空会因为没有工作来找他的麻烦。所以有一天他叫孙悟空来见他。孙悟空来了但没有向玉皇大帝鞠躬。他刚走进来就问，“玉皇大帝，你准备了什么礼物给我这只老猴子？”

sentences.text: 玉皇大帝很担心孙悟空会因为没有工作来找他的麻烦。
sentences.translation: The Jade Emperor was very worried that Sun Wukong would come to him for trouble because he had no job.
sentences.explanation: The sentence showcases the worry of the Jade Emperor regarding Sun Wukong's potential troublemaking due to his lack of a job. The structure '因为...会...' indicates the cause and effect relationship, where '因为' means 'because' and '会' indicates a future action.

sentences.text: 所以有一天他叫孙悟空来见他。
sentences.translation: So one day he asked Sun Wukong to come see him.
sentences.explanation: The structure '叫...来见...' means 'asked...to come see...'.

sentences.text: 孙悟空来了但没有向玉皇大帝鞠躬。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong came but did not bow to the Jade Emperor.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure follows the pattern 'subject + verb + conjunction + negative + indirect object + verb'. The phrase '向玉皇大帝鞠躬' means 'bow to the Jade Emperor'.

sentences.text: 他刚走进来就问，“玉皇大帝，你准备了什么礼物给我这只老猴子？
sentences.translation: He just walked in and asked, 'Jade Emperor, what gift have you prepared for this old monkey of mine?'
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject-Verb-Object. The use of '了' indicates completion of an action, and '给' is used to indicate the recipient of the gift.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 玉皇大帝说，“我没有礼物给你，但是我有一个工作给你。请你照顾仙桃园。这是一个很重要的工作。每天都要小心照顾！”

sentences.text: 玉皇大帝说，“我没有礼物给你，但是我有一个工作给你。
sentences.translation: The Jade Emperor said, "I have no gift for you, but I have a job for you."
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces the Jade Emperor speaking and offering a job instead of a gift, showcasing a cultural aspect of assigning tasks as a form of honor or responsibility.

sentences.text: 请你照顾仙桃园。
sentences.translation: Please take care of the Peach Blossom Garden.
sentences.explanation: The structure '请你' is a polite way to make a request, and '照顾' means 'to take care of'. '仙桃园' refers to the specific location 'Peach Blossom Garden'.

sentences.text: 这是一个很重要的工作。
sentences.translation: This is a very important job.
sentences.explanation: The tricky grammar structure here is the use of the particle '的' to indicate an attributive relationship between '很重要' (very important) and '工作' (job).

sentences.text: 每天都要小心照顾！
sentences.translation: Be careful every day!
sentences.explanation: The structure '每天都要' is a common way to emphasize the necessity of doing something regularly in Chinese.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark, indicating the end of a quote or dialogue.

content.raw_text: 孙悟空很喜欢这个工作，马上就跑到仙桃园。他看了看四周。花园很美很香，每一个地方都可以看到美丽的小树，上面开着美丽的花，还有像金球那样大的水果。

sentences.text: 孙悟空很喜欢这个工作，马上就跑到仙桃园。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong really likes this job and immediately runs to the Peach Garden.
sentences.explanation: The structure '马上就' indicates an immediate action following the previous one.

sentences.text: 他看了看四周。
sentences.translation: He looked around.
sentences.explanation: The tricky part here is the use of the particle '了' after the verb '看', which indicates the completion of the action of looking around.

sentences.text: 花园很美很香，每一个地方都可以看到美丽的小树，上面开着美丽的花，还有像金球那样大的水果。
sentences.translation: The garden is very beautiful and fragrant, you can see beautiful little trees everywhere, with beautiful flowers blooming on them, and fruits as big as golden balls.
sentences.explanation: This sentence describes the beauty of a garden with small trees, flowers, and large fruits. Pay attention to the use of '每一个' meaning 'every' and the structure '像...那样' meaning 'like...'.

content.raw_text: 仙桃园里的土地神告诉孙悟空，仙桃园里有3600棵桃树。前面1200棵树上的小桃需要3000年的时间才能吃，如果吃了它们就会变成神仙。中间1200棵树上的甜桃需要6000年的时间才能吃，如果吃了它们就可以进天宫，长生不老。后面1200棵树上美丽的紫桃需要9000年才能吃，如果吃了它们就会活得像天地、太阳、月亮那样长。

sentences.text: 仙桃园里的土地神告诉孙悟空，仙桃园里有3600棵桃树。
sentences.translation: The land god in the Peach Garden told Sun Wukong that there are 3600 peach trees in the Peach Garden.
sentences.explanation: The structure '里' followed by a noun indicates 'inside' or 'within'. The measure word '棵' is used for counting trees.

sentences.text: 前面1200棵树上的小桃需要3000年的时间才能吃，如果吃了它们就会变成神仙。
sentences.translation: It takes 3000 years to eat the peaches on the 1200 trees in front, and if eaten, they will turn into immortals.
sentences.explanation: The structure '如果...就...' is a common way to express 'if...then...' in Chinese.

sentences.text: 中间1200棵树上的甜桃需要6000年的时间才能吃，如果吃了它们就可以进天宫，长生不老。
sentences.translation: It takes 6000 years to eat the sweet peaches on the 1200 trees in the middle, and if you eat them, you can enter the heavenly palace and live forever.
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes the time it takes to eat the sweet peaches on the trees and the reward of entering the heavenly palace and living forever.

sentences.text: 后面1200棵树上美丽的紫桃需要9000年才能吃，如果吃了它们就会活得像天地，太阳，月亮那样长。
sentences.translation: The beautiful purple peaches on the 1200 trees behind need 9000 years to ripen. If eaten, one will live as long as the heavens, the sun, and the moon.
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes the long ripening time of the purple peaches on the trees and the longevity one may achieve by consuming them.

content.raw_text: 孙悟空爱上了仙桃园。他什么地方都不去了，也不去找他的朋友了。他每天都在仙桃园里。有一天他看到一些桃子已经能吃了。他非常想吃一个，但他不能那样做，因为有园工在仙桃园里，他不想让他们看到他吃桃子。所以他让园工先离开仙桃园。只留他一个人了！他爬上树，吃了一个桃子。非常好吃，他又吃了一个，然后又是一个，他一直在吃，最后他吃得太饱了。

sentences.text: 孙悟空爱上了仙桃园。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong fell in love with the Peach Garden.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Verb + Object. The tricky part might be the word '了' which indicates the completion of an action in this context.

sentences.text: 他什么地方都不去了，也不去找他的朋友了。
sentences.translation: He didn't go anywhere, nor did he go to find his friends.
sentences.explanation: This sentence uses the structure '什么地方都不去' to emphasize that he didn't go anywhere at all. The repetition of '不去' emphasizes the negation of going, and '也不去' adds on to say he also didn't go to find his friends.

sentences.text: 他每天都在仙桃园里。
sentences.translation: He is in the fairy peach garden every day.
sentences.explanation: The structure '每天都' emphasizes the frequency of the action, meaning 'every day'. The phrase '仙桃园' is a specific location, 'fairy peach garden'.

sentences.text: 有一天他看到一些桃子已经能吃了。
sentences.translation: One day he saw that some peaches were already ripe and ready to eat.
sentences.explanation: The structure '已经...了' is used to indicate that something has already happened or is already in a certain state.

sentences.text: 他非常想吃一个，但他不能那样做，因为有园工在仙桃园里，他不想让他们看到他吃桃子。
sentences.translation: He really wanted to eat one, but he couldn't do that because there were gardeners in the peach garden, and he didn't want them to see him eating peaches.
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces the desire of the character to eat a peach, but he refrains from doing so because there are gardeners in the peach garden whom he doesn't want to see him eating the peaches.

sentences.text: 所以他让园工先离开仙桃园。
sentences.translation: So he asked the garden worker to leave Xiantao Garden first.
sentences.explanation: The structure '让...先...' indicates asking someone to do something before others.

sentences.text: 只留他一个人了！
sentences.translation: Only him left!
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese can be different from English, with the verb often placed before the subject. In this case, the sentence is emphasizing that only one person (him) is left.

words.definition: indicates completion or change of state

sentences.text: 他爬上树，吃了一个桃子。
sentences.translation: He climbed up the tree and ate a peach.
sentences.explanation: The structure '吃了' indicates that the action of eating is completed.

sentences.text: 非常好吃，他又吃了一个，然后又是一个，他一直在吃，最后他吃得太饱了。
sentences.translation: It's very delicious. He ate another one, then another one. He kept eating, and in the end, he ate too much.
sentences.explanation: The structure '又...又...' is used to indicate a repeated action. The use of '得' in '吃得太饱了' is a common way to express 'too much' or 'to the point of' in Chinese.

content.raw_text: 几天以后，王母娘娘（就是玉皇大帝的妈妈）决定开一个宴会。她想要在宴会上放一些仙桃。她让她的七衣仙女，红衣仙女、蓝衣仙女、白衣仙女、黑衣仙女、紫衣仙女、黄衣仙女和绿衣仙女去摘一些仙桃。仙女们去了仙桃园，但是仙桃园里的土地神让她们等着。“今年跟去年不同，”他说。“今年我们有一个新的大臣，齐天大圣。我必须先告诉他你们来了。”

sentences.text: 几天以后，王母娘娘（就是玉皇大帝的妈妈）决定开一个宴会。
sentences.translation: A few days later, the Queen Mother of the West (who is the mother of the Jade Emperor) decided to hold a banquet.
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces the Queen Mother of the West, who is a figure in Chinese mythology. The structure '就是' is used to explain or define something, similar to 'who is' in English.

sentences.text: 她想要在宴会上放一些仙桃。
sentences.translation: She wants to put some peaches at the banquet.
sentences.explanation: The structure '在...上' is used to indicate the location where an action takes place. 一些 means 'some' in this context.

sentences.text: 她让她的七衣仙女，红衣仙女，蓝衣仙女，白衣仙女，黑衣仙女，紫衣仙女，黄衣仙女和绿衣仙女去摘一些仙桃。
sentences.translation: She asked her seven fairy maidens, the red fairy, the blue fairy, the white fairy, the black fairy, the purple fairy, the yellow fairy, and the green fairy, to pick some fairy peaches.
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces a list of fairy maidens with different colored clothing, a common motif in Chinese folklore. The structure of listing items using '、' before the last item and '和' before the verb '去' is a common pattern in Chinese grammar.

sentences.text: 仙女们去了仙桃园，但是仙桃园里的土地神让她们等着。
sentences.translation: The fairies went to the fairy peach garden, but the land god in the fairy peach garden made them wait.
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces the concept of a 'land god' (土地神) which may be unfamiliar to some learners. It also demonstrates the possessive particle '的' used to indicate possession or association.

sentences.text: “今年跟去年不同，”他说。
sentences.translation: This year is different from last year,
sentences.explanation: The structure '今年跟去年不同' means 'this year is different from last year.' The use of '跟' here indicates a comparison between two time periods.

sentences.text: “今年我们有一个新的大臣，齐天大圣。
sentences.translation: This year we have a new minister, the Great Sage Equal to Heaven.
sentences.explanation: The phrase '齐天大圣' refers to Sun Wukong, a character from the Chinese classical novel 'Journey to the West'. This sentence introduces a new minister with a reference to this famous mythical figure.

sentences.text: 我必须先告诉他你们来了。
sentences.translation: I must first tell him that you guys have come.
sentences.explanation: The structure '先告诉' means 'first tell', which is a common way to express the order of actions in Chinese.
The sentence contains a closing quotation mark and an ellipsis, indicating that there is more text following this sentence.

content.raw_text: “他在哪儿？”她们问。

sentences.text: “他在哪儿？
sentences.translation: Where is he?
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a question asking for the location of a person. 哪儿 (nǎr) is a colloquial way of saying "where" in Mandarin Chinese.

sentences.text: ”她们问。
sentences.translation: They asked.
sentences.explanation: The sentence consists of a quotation mark followed by the pronoun 'they' and the verb 'ask'.

content.raw_text: “在仙桃园里。他累了，在睡觉。”

sentences.text: “在仙桃园里。
sentences.translation: In the fairy peach garden.
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes a location, indicating that something is inside the fairy peach garden.

sentences.text: 他累了，在睡觉。
sentences.translation: He is tired, going to sleep.
sentences.explanation: The structure 在 + verb indicates an ongoing action, in this case, the action of sleeping.

words.definition: indicating completion or change of situation

sentences.translation: Chapter 5
sentences.explanation: The sentence simply states the chapter number in Chinese.

content.raw_text: “王母娘娘让我们来这里摘桃子。我们不能太晚了，我们现在去见他。”

sentences.text: “王母娘娘让我们来这里摘桃子。
sentences.translation: Queen Mother asked us to come here to pick peaches.
sentences.explanation: In Chinese culture, '王母娘娘' refers to the Queen Mother of the West, a goddess in Taoism. The structure '让...来...' is used to indicate someone asking or telling someone to come and do something.

sentences.text: 我们不能太晚了，我们现在去见他。
sentences.translation: We cannot be too late, let's go see him now.
sentences.explanation: The structure '太...了' is used to indicate 'too much' or 'too late' in this context. The word '了' here indicates a change in the situation, showing that the action of being late has been completed.

words.definition: (particle indicating completion or change of situation)

sentences.explanation: The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 仙女们和土地神走进了仙桃园，但找不到孙悟空。他吃了很多桃子，太饱了，所以他把自己变成二寸长，在树上睡着了。

sentences.text: 仙女们和土地神走进了仙桃园，但找不到孙悟空。
sentences.translation: The fairies and the earth gods entered the Peach Blossom Garden, but could not find Sun Wukong.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure follows a common pattern in Chinese where the subject is followed by the action and then the location. The use of '了' indicates the completion of an action.

sentences.text: 他吃了很多桃子，太饱了，所以他把自己变成二寸长，在树上睡着了。
sentences.translation: He ate a lot of peaches, got too full, so he turned himself into two inches long and fell asleep on the tree.
sentences.explanation: The structure '把...变成' is a common way to express 'turn into' in Chinese.

words.definition: (particle marking the object of a verb)

content.raw_text: 仙女们说，“是王母娘娘让我们来摘仙桃的。所以大圣在我们要摘，大圣不在我们也要摘。”

sentences.text: 仙女们说，“是王母娘娘让我们来摘仙桃的。
sentences.translation: The fairies said, 'It is the Queen Mother of the West who asked us to pick the peaches of immortality.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Object. The term '王母娘娘' refers to the Queen Mother of the West, a figure in Chinese mythology known for her association with peaches of immortality.

sentences.text: 所以大圣在我们要摘，大圣不在我们也要摘。
sentences.translation: So, the Great Sage, whether he is with us or not, we must pick.
sentences.explanation: The structure '不在我们也要' emphasizes the necessity of picking the Great Sage regardless of whether he is present or not.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 他们开始摘已经可以吃的仙桃，但是只能找到一点点，因为孙悟空吃了很多。仙女们看到一棵树上有一只已经可以吃的仙桃，孙悟空正好睡在那棵树上。当蓝衣仙女和红衣仙女一起把桃子摘下来的时候，树动了，孙悟空从树上掉了下来。他醒了，马上变回到自己的样子。他从耳朵里拿出金箍棒，把它变成像碗那么粗。

sentences.text: 他们开始摘已经可以吃的仙桃，但是只能找到一点点，因为孙悟空吃了很多。
sentences.translation: They began picking the ripe peaches that were ready to eat, but could only find a little bit because Sun Wukong had eaten a lot.
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces the action of picking ripe peaches and highlights the fact that there were only a few left because Sun Wukong had eaten most of them.

sentences.text: 仙女们看到一棵树上有一只已经可以吃的仙桃，孙悟空正好睡在那棵树上。
sentences.translation: The fairies saw a ripe peach on a tree, and Sun Wukong happened to be sleeping on that tree.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the use of measure words in Chinese, such as 棵 for trees and 只 for animals. It also demonstrates the adjectival marker 的 to indicate possession.

sentences.text: 当蓝衣仙女和红衣仙女一起把桃子摘下来的时候，树动了孙悟空从树上掉了下来。
sentences.translation: When the blue fairy and the red fairy picked the peaches together, the tree moved, and Sun Wukong fell from the tree.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the use of the verb-object structure in Chinese, where the object is placed before the verb. It also includes the time-indicating phrase '的时候' to indicate when an action took place.

words.definition: indicating the object of the verb

sentences.text: 他醒了，马上变回到自己的样子。
sentences.translation: He woke up and immediately turned back to his own appearance.
sentences.explanation: The structure '变回' means 'turn back to' in this context. It's a common way to express returning to a previous state or appearance.

sentences.text: 他从耳朵里拿出金箍棒，把它变成像碗那么粗。
sentences.translation: He took the golden hoop rod out of his ear and turned it into something as thick as a bowl.
sentences.explanation: This sentence contains a common structure in Chinese where the object is placed before the verb, as in '把它变成' (turn it into). Also, the comparison '像...那么...' is used to indicate similarity in this context.

content.raw_text: 他大喊，“你们这些妖怪，你们从哪里来，为什么要拿我的桃子？”

sentences.text: 他大喊，“你们这些妖怪，你们从哪里来，为什么要拿我的桃子？
sentences.translation: He shouted, 'You monsters, where did you come from, why are you taking my peaches?'
sentences.explanation: The sentence contains a question structure with '从...来' (come from) and '为什么' (why).
The sentence contains a closing quotation mark and an ellipsis, which indicates a pause or omission in the text.

content.raw_text: 仙女们非常害怕，说，“很对不起，大圣！我们不是妖怪。我们是七衣仙女，王母娘娘让我们来为宴会摘一些仙桃。我们知道这是你照顾的仙桃园，我们找过你，但是没有找到。请原谅我们！”

sentences.text: 仙女们非常害怕，说“很对不起，大圣！
sentences.translation: The fairies were very scared and said, 'I'm so sorry, Great Sage!'
sentences.explanation: The phrase '大圣' is a respectful term used to address the Monkey King, a legendary figure in Chinese mythology.

sentences.text: 我们不是妖怪。
sentences.translation: We are not monsters.
sentences.explanation: The structure '不是' is used to negate the following noun '妖怪' (monsters).

sentences.text: 我们是七衣仙女，王母娘娘让我们来为宴会摘一些仙桃。
sentences.translation: We are the Seven Fairy Maidens. Queen Mother sent us to pick some fairy peaches for the banquet.
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces the Seven Fairy Maidens who were sent by Queen Mother to pick fairy peaches for a banquet. The structure '让我们来为' indicates that they were sent to do something.

sentences.text: 我们知道这是你照顾的仙桃园，我们找过你，但是没有找到。
sentences.translation: We know this is the peach garden you take care of, we have looked for you, but did not find.
sentences.explanation: The structure '找过' indicates that the action of looking for someone has been done in the past.

sentences.text: 请原谅我们！
sentences.translation: Please forgive us!
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a polite request for forgiveness, using the word '请' to indicate politeness.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 孙悟空不再生气了，他想到了宴会就笑了起来。“谢谢你们来请我参加这个宴会！” 他说。

sentences.text: 孙悟空不再生气了，他想到了宴会就笑了起来。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong was no longer angry, he smiled when he thought of the banquet.
sentences.explanation: The structure '想到了' means 'thought of' and '笑了起来' means 'smiled'. Pay attention to the use of particles like '了' to indicate changes in the situation or completion of actions.

words.definition: particle indicating a change of situation or completion of an action
particle indicating a change of situation or completion of an action
particle indicating a change of situation or completion of an action

sentences.text: “谢谢你们来请我参加这个宴会！
sentences.translation: Thank you for inviting me to this banquet!
sentences.explanation: The structure '请我参加' means 'invite me to participate' and might be confusing for learners due to the different word order compared to English.

sentences.text: ” 他说。
sentences.translation: He said.
sentences.explanation: This sentence consists of the pronoun '他' meaning 'he' and the verb '说' meaning 'said'. The quotation mark '”' indicates the beginning of reported speech, and the period '。' marks the end of the sentence.

content.raw_text: 仙女们不知道孙悟空在讲什么，她们说，“很对不起，在参加宴会的名字中，我们没有听到你的名字，所以我们不知道是不是请了你。”

sentences.text: 仙女们不知道孙悟空在讲什么，她们说，“很对不起，在参加宴会的名字中，我们没有听到你的名字，所以我们不知道是不是请了你。
sentences.translation: The fairies don't know what Sun Wukong is talking about. They say, 'We are very sorry. In the list of guests for the banquet, we did not hear your name, so we do not know if you were invited.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence involves a polite apology and explanation from the fairies to Sun Wukong for not inviting him to the banquet because they did not hear his name on the guest list.
The sentence ends with a quotation mark and an ellipsis, indicating that there is more to come or something is left unsaid.

content.raw_text: “没问题，”孙悟空说，“我这老猴子会知道是不是请了我。等在这里！”然后他在七衣仙女身上用了魔法，仙女们就不能动了。他一个筋斗云去了宴会的地方。路上，他遇到了一个漂亮的年轻人，和他向同一个方向走去。他问了那个人的名字和他要去的地方。

sentences.text: “没问题，”孙悟空说，“我这老猴子会知道是不是请了我。
sentences.translation: No problem,
sentences.explanation: The sentence includes a complex structure with the verb '知道' (to know) followed by '是不是' (whether or not), which together mean 'know whether'. The use of '了' at the end of the sentence indicates the completion of the action of inviting.

sentences.text: 等在这里！
sentences.translation: Wait here!
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is straightforward, with the verb '等' (wait) followed by the location '在这里' (here). The exclamation mark '！' adds emphasis to the command.

sentences.text: ”然后他在七衣仙女身上用了魔法，仙女们就不能动了。
sentences.translation: Then he used magic on the seven fairy's bodies, and the fairies couldn't move.
sentences.explanation: The structure '在...身上用' means 'use on the bodies of...'. The use of '了' indicates the completion of an action.

sentences.text: 他一个筋斗云去了宴会的地方。
sentences.translation: He flew on a somersault cloud to the place of the banquet.
sentences.explanation: The phrase '筋斗云' refers to a magical cloud in Chinese mythology that allows the user to fly through the air.

sentences.text: 路上，他遇到了一个漂亮的年轻人，和他向同一个方向走去。
sentences.translation: On the way, he met a handsome young man, walking in the same direction as him.
sentences.explanation: The structure '和他向同一个方向走去' means 'walking in the same direction as him', where '和' is used to connect two subjects.

sentences.text: 他问了那个人的名字和他要去的地方。
sentences.translation: He asked for the name of that person and the place he was going to.
sentences.explanation: The structure '和' is used to connect two nouns, similar to 'and' in English.

content.raw_text: “我是赤脚大仙，”漂亮的年轻人说，“我要去那仙桃宴会。”

sentences.text: “我是赤脚大仙，”漂亮的年轻人说，我要去那仙桃宴会。
sentences.translation: I am the Barefoot Immortal," the handsome young man said, "I am going to that Immortal Peach Banquet.
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces a character who identifies himself as the 'Barefoot Immortal' and mentions his intention to attend the 'Immortal Peach Banquet'. The use of quotation marks indicates direct speech.
This sentence only contains a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 孙悟空说，“啊，你走错路了！今年的宴会是在通明宫。玉皇大帝让我告诉大家。”

sentences.text: 孙悟空说，“啊，你走错路了！
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong said, "Ah, you've taken the wrong path!"
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Verb + Object. The use of '了' at the end of the sentence indicates the completion of the action of taking the wrong path.

sentences.text: 今年的宴会是在通明宫。
sentences.translation: This year's banquet is at Tongming Palace.
sentences.explanation: The structure '在 + location' is used to indicate the location of an action or event in Chinese.

sentences.text: 玉皇大帝让我告诉大家。
sentences.translation: The Jade Emperor asked me to tell everyone.
sentences.explanation: The tricky part here might be the use of '让' which can mean 'asked' or 'let' depending on the context. In this sentence, it means 'asked'.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: “我不知道！”赤脚大仙说,然后他向另一个方向走了。孙悟空把自己变成赤脚大仙的样子，一个筋斗云到了宴会的地方。

sentences.text: “我不知道！
sentences.translation: I don't know!
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a simple statement expressing lack of knowledge. The word order in Chinese is Subject + 不 + Verb, which is different from English.

sentences.text: ”赤脚大仙说，然后他向另一个方向走了。
sentences.translation: The Barefoot Immortal said, then he walked in another direction.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject-Verb-Object, and the particle '了' is used to indicate completion of an action.

sentences.text: 孙悟空把自己变成赤脚大仙的样子，一个筋斗云到了宴会的地方。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong transformed himself into the appearance of the Barefoot Immortal and flew on a somersault cloud to the banquet.
sentences.explanation: The sentence showcases the use of the particle '把' to indicate the object of the verb, as well as the possessive particle '的' to show possession. The concept of transforming into someone's appearance and using a somersault cloud for transportation may be unfamiliar to learners.

words.definition: indicating the object of the verb

content.raw_text: 他是第一个来到宴会的客人，已经有几个工人在那里准备吃的东西。他看了一下四周，看到了一百多种不同的好吃的东西。然后他闻到香香的葡萄酒。孙悟空又饿又渴，他真的很想吃那些东西，喝点美酒！但是他不能，因为其他的人会看到他。怎么办呢？他用魔法变出一群虫子。虫子飞了过去咬了所有的人，这些人就都睡着了。

sentences.text: 他是第一个来到宴会的客人，已经有几个工人在那里准备吃的东西。
sentences.translation: He is the first guest to arrive at the banquet, and there are already several workers there preparing food.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the use of the possessive particle '的' to indicate possession in Chinese. It also demonstrates the word order in Chinese sentences, where the subject usually comes before the verb.

sentences.text: 他看了一下四周，看到了一百多种不同的好吃的东西。
sentences.translation: He looked around, seeing over a hundred different delicious things.
sentences.explanation: The structure '一百多' means 'over a hundred' in this context. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate the relationship between the adjective '好吃' (delicious) and the noun '东西' (things).

sentences.text: 然后他闻到香香的葡萄酒。
sentences.translation: Then he smelled the fragrant wine.
sentences.explanation: The structure '闻到' means 'to smell' in this context. The repetition of '香' emphasizes the fragrance of the wine.

sentences.text: 孙悟空又饿又渴，他真的很想吃那些东西，喝点美酒！
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong is both hungry and thirsty, he really wants to eat those things and drink some fine wine!
sentences.explanation: The structure '又...又...' is used to express 'both...and...' in Chinese. In this sentence, it emphasizes that Sun Wukong is both hungry and thirsty.

sentences.text: 但是他不能，因为其他的人会看到他。
sentences.translation: But he can't, because other people will see him.
sentences.explanation: The structure '因为...会...' is used to indicate the reason for an action and the result that will follow.

sentences.text: 怎么办呢？
sentences.translation: What should we do?
sentences.explanation: The sentence is a question asking for advice or suggestions on what to do in a certain situation.

words.definition: (particle indicating a question or emphasizing a point)

sentences.text: 他用魔法变出一群虫子。
sentences.translation: He used magic to conjure a group of insects.
sentences.explanation: The structure '用...变出' means 'to use...to conjure' in this context.

sentences.text: 虫子飞了过去咬了所有的人，这些人就都睡着了。
sentences.translation: The insects flew over and bit all the people, so they all fell asleep.
sentences.explanation: The sentence showcases the use of 了 to indicate completion of actions and the possessive particle 的. The structure '就都' is a common way to express 'then all' in Chinese.

content.raw_text: 现在，孙悟空一个人在那里对着好吃的东西和香香的葡萄酒。他吃了很多很多，吃得很饱很饱，他喝了很多酒，喝得很醉很醉。然后他想，“坏猴子！坏猴子！人们很快就会到这里，我会有很大的麻烦。我现在必须要离开这里！”

sentences.text: 现在，孙悟空一个人在那里对着好吃的东西和香香的葡萄酒。
sentences.translation: Now, Sun Wukong is there alone, facing delicious food and fragrant wine.
sentences.explanation: The structure '对着' indicates facing or towards something, and '香香的' is a reduplication to emphasize the fragrance of the wine.

sentences.text: 他吃了很多很多，吃得很饱很饱，他喝了很多酒，喝得很醉很醉。
sentences.translation: He ate a lot, ate until very full, he drank a lot of alcohol, drank until very drunk.
sentences.explanation: This sentence uses the structure 'verb + 得 + adjective' to indicate the degree or result of an action. For example, '吃得很饱' means 'ate until very full' and '喝得很醉' means 'drank until very drunk'.

sentences.text: 然后他想，“坏猴子！
sentences.translation: Then he thought, 'Bad monkey!'
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is straightforward, but the use of quotation marks '坏猴子' within the sentence indicates direct speech or thoughts of the character.

sentences.text: 坏猴子！
sentences.translation: Bad monkey!
sentences.explanation: The sentence consists of two words '坏' meaning 'bad' and '猴子' meaning 'monkey', followed by an exclamation mark '！'. It is a simple and direct expression to describe a mischievous or naughty monkey.

sentences.text: 人们很快就会到这里，我会有很大的麻烦。
sentences.translation: People will arrive here soon, and I will have a lot of trouble.
sentences.explanation: The structure '会...的' is used to indicate a future event or situation that is certain to happen.

sentences.text: 我现在必须要离开这里！
sentences.translation: I must leave here now!
sentences.explanation: The structure '必须要' is used to emphasize the necessity of an action in Chinese.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 但是，对孙悟空来说，情况变得更坏了。他太醉了，找不到回家的路了。他发现自己不在家里而是在太上老君住的地方。

sentences.text: 但是，对孙悟空来说，情况变得更坏了。
sentences.translation: However, for Sun Wukong, the situation became even worse.
sentences.explanation: The structure '对...来说' is used to indicate 'for' someone in this context.

sentences.text: 他太醉了，找不到回家的路了。
sentences.translation: He was too drunk to find his way home.
sentences.explanation: The structure '找不到' means 'unable to find'. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate 'way home'.

words.definition: indicating completion or change of state
indicating completion or change of state

sentences.text: 他发现自己不在家里而是在太上老君住的地方。
sentences.translation: He found himself not at home but at the place where Laozi lived.
sentences.explanation: The structure '不在...而是在...' is used to express 'not at...but at...' in Chinese.

content.raw_text: “好吧，”孙悟空想，“虽然我很想回家，但现在我已经在这里了。我一直想见见这位老君。现在正好可以见见他了！”

sentences.text: “好吧，”孙悟空想，“虽然我很想回家，但现在我已经在这里了。
sentences.translation: Well,
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure involves expressing conflicting desires using '虽然...但' (although...but) and indicating completion of an action with '了'.

words.definition: modal particle indicating suggestion or softening
Sun Wukong (name of the Monkey King)

sentences.text: 我一直想见见这位老君。
sentences.translation: I have always wanted to meet this Laojun.
sentences.explanation: The structure '一直想' indicates a continuous desire or wish, and '这位' is used before a person's name or title to show respect.

sentences.text: 现在正好可以见见他了！
sentences.translation: Now is a good time to meet him!
sentences.explanation: The structure '可以 + verb' is used to express permission or ability in this context. The repetition of the verb '见' emphasizes the action of meeting.

words.definition: indicates a completed action or change

sentences.explanation: The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 但是太上老君不在家。他出去讲课了。孙悟空看了所有的房间，没有找到太上老君。但是他发现了五瓶长生不老的金丹。太上老君准备在宴会上把这些金丹送给客人，让他们长生不老。

sentences.text: 但是太上老君不在家。
sentences.translation: But Laozi is not at home.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure follows the pattern of subject + negation + location. The term '太上老君' refers to Laozi, a central figure in Taoism.

sentences.text: 他出去讲课了。
sentences.translation: He went out to give a lecture.
sentences.explanation: The structure '出去' followed by a verb indicates the action of going out to do something. The particle '了' at the end of the sentence indicates the completion of the action.

sentences.text: 孙悟空看了所有的房间，没有找到太上老君。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong looked at all the rooms and did not find Taishang Laojun.
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure follows a common pattern in Chinese where the subject is followed by the verb and then the object. The use of particles like '了' and '的' are essential in Chinese grammar.

words.definition: Sun (referring to 孙悟空 Sun Wukong)
Taishang Laojun (a deity in Chinese mythology)

sentences.text: 但是他发现了五瓶长生不老的金丹。
sentences.translation: But he discovered five bottles of golden pills for immortality.
sentences.explanation: The phrase '长生不老' is a common idiom in Chinese referring to immortality or eternal youth.

sentences.text: 太上老君准备在宴会上把这些金丹送给客人，让他们长生不老。
sentences.translation: The Supreme Old Lord is preparing to give these golden elixirs to the guests at the banquet, allowing them to live forever.
sentences.explanation: The structure '让...长生不老' means 'allow them to live forever'. This sentence introduces the concept of '金丹' (golden elixirs) which is a traditional Chinese alchemical substance believed to grant immortality.

content.raw_text: 那孙悟空又做了些什么呢？当然了，他吃了所有的金丹！但现在他真的很害怕，他想，“坏了！坏了！我给自己找了很大的麻烦。

sentences.text: 那孙悟空又做了些什么呢？
sentences.translation: What did Sun Wukong do again?
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + 又 + Verb + 了 + Measure Word + 什么 + 呢. The use of 又 indicates the action is done again, and 了 indicates completion of the action.

words.definition: (used at the end of a sentence to express an inquiry)

sentences.text: 当然了，他吃了所有的金丹！
sentences.translation: Of course, he ate all the golden pills!
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Object. The use of 了 indicates the completion of the action of eating.

sentences.text: 但现在他真的很害怕，他想，“坏了！
sentences.translation: But now he was really scared, he thought, 'Oh no!'
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Adverb + Verb. The use of quotation marks '“' and '”' indicates direct speech.

sentences.text: 坏了！
sentences.translation: Broken!
sentences.explanation: The sentence expresses that something is broken or in a bad state.

sentences.text: 我给自己找了很大的麻烦。
sentences.translation: I caused myself a lot of trouble.
sentences.explanation: The structure '给...找...' means 'cause/find trouble for oneself'. The possessive particle '的' is used to indicate the relationship between '大' (big) and '麻烦' (trouble).

content.raw_text: 如果玉皇大帝知道了，他会杀了我的！”他跑出了太上老君的房子，一个筋斗云回到了他花果山的家。

sentences.text: 如果玉皇大帝知道了，他会杀了我的！
sentences.translation: If the Jade Emperor finds out, he will kill me!
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is '如果...，他会...'. The use of '了' after a verb indicates the completion of an action.

sentences.text: ”他跑出了太上老君的房子，一个筋斗云回到了他花果山的家。
sentences.translation: He ran out of Taishang Laojun's house, did a somersault cloud, and returned to his home on Flower Fruit Mountain.
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes a character running out of a deity's house, using a magical cloud to return to his home on Flower Fruit Mountain.

words.definition: Taishang Laojun (a deity in Chinese mythology)
somersault cloud (a magical cloud in Chinese mythology)

content.raw_text: 花果山的猴子们看到他们的大王都很高兴。他们说，“大王，你已经走了一百多年了。你去了哪里，你做了什么？”

sentences.text: 花果山的猴子们看到他们的大王都很高兴。
sentences.translation: The monkeys of Flower Fruit Mountain were very happy to see their king.
sentences.explanation: The structure '都很' is used to emphasize that all of the monkeys were very happy.

sentences.text: 他们说，“大王，你已经走了一百多年了。
sentences.translation: They said, "Great King, you have been gone for over a hundred years."
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject-Verb-Object. The use of "了" at the end of the sentence indicates a completed action or change of state.

words.definition: indicating completion or change of state

sentences.text: 你去了哪里，你做了什么？
sentences.translation: Where did you go, what did you do?
sentences.explanation: This sentence is a simple question asking about someone's whereabouts and actions. Pay attention to the use of 了 after verbs to indicate completion of an action.
This sentence is missing the actual content, but it ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 虽然孙悟空在天宫里只有几个月，但是天上的一天就是地上的一年。

sentences.text: 虽然孙悟空在天宫里只有几个月，但是天上的一天就是地上的一年。
sentences.translation: Although Sun Wukong only spent a few months in the Heavenly Palace, one day in the sky is equivalent to a year on earth.
sentences.explanation: The structure '天上的一天就是地上的一年' is a comparison structure indicating the time difference between the sky and the earth.

content.raw_text: 他说，“我很高兴地告诉你们，玉皇大帝给了我齐天大圣的工作，这是一个很好的工作，照顾仙桃园。我一开始吃了一个桃子，发现它很好吃，所以我又吃了很多很多。然后我又去了一个宴会，虽然他们没有请我去。在宴会上我吃了很多东西，喝了很多酒。我喝醉了，发现自己在太上老君的房子里，在那里我吃了五瓶他的金丹。我害怕玉皇大帝会听到这些事，所以我很快就回家来了。”

sentences.text: 他说，“我很高兴地告诉你们，玉皇大帝给了我齐天大圣的工作，这是一个很好的工作，照顾仙桃园。
sentences.translation: He said, 'I am happy to tell you that the Jade Emperor has given me the job of the Great Sage Equal to Heaven, which is a very good job, taking care of the Peach Garden.'
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces the character boasting about being appointed as the Great Sage Equal to Heaven by the Jade Emperor, a significant role in Chinese mythology. The phrase '照顾仙桃园' means 'taking care of the Peach Garden', which is a reference to a specific task in the story.

sentences.text: 我一开始吃了一个桃子，发现它很好吃，所以我又吃了很多很多。
sentences.translation: At first, I ate a peach and found it very delicious, so I ate a lot more.
sentences.explanation: The structure '又...又...' is used to indicate a repeated action or state. In this sentence, the speaker ate a peach, found it delicious, and then ate a lot more.

sentences.text: 然后我又去了一个宴会，虽然他们没有请我去。
sentences.translation: Then I went to another banquet, although they did not invite me.
sentences.explanation: The structure '虽然...但是...' is commonly used to express 'although...but...' in Chinese.

sentences.text: 在宴会上我吃了很多东西，喝了很多酒。
sentences.translation: At the banquet, I ate a lot of food and drank a lot of wine.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the use of the verb '吃' (to eat) and '喝' (to drink) in the context of consuming food and drinks at a banquet.

sentences.text: 我喝醉了，发现自己在太上老君的房子里，在那里我吃了五瓶他的金丹。
sentences.translation: I got drunk and found myself in the house of Laozi, where I ate five bottles of his golden elixir.
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes a scenario where the speaker got drunk and unexpectedly found themselves in the house of Laozi, where they consumed five bottles of his golden elixir.

sentences.text: 我害怕玉皇大帝会听到这些事，所以我很快就回家来了。
sentences.translation: I'm afraid the Jade Emperor will hear about these things, so I quickly went home.
sentences.explanation: The structure '所以' (so) is used to indicate a cause-and-effect relationship in the sentence. The word '就' (then) is used to express the immediacy of the action that follows.
This sentence is missing text, only containing a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: 猴子们很爱他们的大王，所以他们为他准备了一个宴会，还给了他一杯他们自己做的酒。孙悟空喝了一口，但是马上吐了出来。“这酒太难喝了！”他说。

sentences.text: 猴子们很爱他们的大王，所以他们为他准备了一个宴会，还给了他一杯他们自己做的酒。
sentences.translation: The monkeys love their king very much, so they prepared a banquet for him and also gave him a cup of wine they made themselves.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the possessive particle '的' used to indicate possession or modification, as well as the particle '了' indicating completion of an action.

words.definition: particle indicating completion of an action
particle indicating completion of an action

sentences.text: 孙悟空喝了一口，但是马上吐了出来。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong took a sip, but immediately spat it out.
sentences.explanation: The structure '了...出来' is used to indicate the completion of an action and the result of that action.

sentences.text: “这酒太难喝了！
sentences.translation: This wine is too hard to drink!
sentences.explanation: The structure '太 + adjective + 了' is used to express that something is too much or too extreme.

words.definition: (particle indicating completion or change of situation)

sentences.text: ”他说。
sentences.translation: He said.
sentences.explanation: This sentence is a simple statement where the subject 他 (he) is followed by the verb 说 (said). The quotation mark at the beginning indicates that someone is speaking.

content.raw_text: 猴子们说，“大王一直在天宫里吃饭喝酒。我们这里吃的喝的当然没有天宫里的东西好！”

sentences.text: 猴子们说，“大王一直在天宫里吃饭喝酒。
sentences.translation: The monkeys said, "The king has been eating and drinking in the heavenly palace."
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure in Chinese is Subject + Verb + Object. The use of 在 indicates the location of an action happening. The phrase '一直在' indicates a continuous action that has been happening.

sentences.text: 我们这里吃的喝的当然没有天宫里的东西好！
sentences.translation: Of course, what we eat and drink here is not as good as what they have in the heavenly palace!
sentences.explanation: The sentence compares the quality of food and drink in two different places, emphasizing that what they have in the heavenly palace is much better than what is available here.
The sentence ends with a closing quotation mark.

content.raw_text: “没问题，”孙悟空说，“我会给你们带回一些好酒的！”然后他跳了起来，一个筋斗云回到了天宫。他去了宴会的地方，拿了四瓶玉皇大帝最好的酒带回了花果山，和他的朋友们一起喝了酒。

sentences.text: “没问题，”孙悟空说，“我会给你们带回一些好酒的！
sentences.translation: No problem,
sentences.explanation: The structure '会给...带回' means 'will bring back' in this context. 孙悟空 is the name 'Sun Wukong', a character from the Chinese classical novel 'Journey to the West'.

sentences.text: ”然后他跳了起来，一个筋斗云回到了天宫。
sentences.translation: Then he jumped up and somersaulted back to the Heavenly Palace.
sentences.explanation: This sentence describes a mythical action where a character jumps up and uses a somersault cloud to return to the Heavenly Palace. The use of the somersault cloud is a common theme in Chinese mythology.

words.definition: somersault cloud (a mythical cloud used for transportation)

sentences.text: 他去了宴会的地方，拿了四瓶玉皇大帝最好的酒带回了花果山，和他的朋友们一起喝了酒。
sentences.translation: He went to the banquet venue, took four bottles of the best wine from the Jade Emperor, brought them back to Flower Fruit Mountain, and drank with his friends.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the use of possessive particles '的' and '了' to indicate completed actions. It also demonstrates the structure of '和...一起' meaning 'together with'.

content.raw_text: 你还记得那七个仙女吗？她们还是在同一个地方！孙悟空的魔法让她们一点都不能动，所以她们一天都站在仙桃园里的一棵树下，要等到魔法结束了，她们才可以再次走动。

sentences.text: 你还记得那七个仙女吗？
sentences.translation: Do you still remember those seven fairies?
sentences.explanation: The structure '还记得' is a common way to ask if someone still remembers something in Chinese.

words.definition: measure word for people or objects

sentences.text: 她们还是在同一个地方！
sentences.translation: They are still in the same place!
sentences.explanation: The sentence structure is Subject + Adverb + Location + Adjective + Noun, which is a common pattern in Chinese sentences.

sentences.text: 孙悟空的魔法让她们一点都不能动，所以她们一天都站在仙桃园里的一棵树下，要等到魔法结束了，她们才可以再次走动。
sentences.translation: Sun Wukong's magic made them unable to move at all, so they stood under a tree in the peach garden all day, waiting for the magic to end before they could move again.
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes how Sun Wukong's magic immobilized the characters, forcing them to wait under a tree in the peach garden until the magic wore off.

content.raw_text: 但是对孙悟空来说，事情变得很不好。先是仙女们告诉王母娘娘，孙悟空吃了很多仙桃，用魔法让她们在花园里不能动。王母娘娘去了她的儿子玉皇大帝那里，告诉他这个事情。

sentences.text: 但是对孙悟空来说，事情变得很不好。
sentences.translation: But for Sun Wukong, things turned very bad.
sentences.explanation: The structure '对...来说' is used to indicate 'for' or 'to' someone in this context. The word '很' is used before an adjective to indicate 'very'.

sentences.text: 先是仙女们告诉王母娘娘，孙悟空吃了很多仙桃，用魔法让她们在花园里不能动。
sentences.translation: First, the fairies told the Queen Mother that Sun Wukong had eaten a lot of fairy peaches and used magic to make them unable to move in the garden.
sentences.explanation: The sentence introduces a sequence of events where the fairies inform the Queen Mother about Sun Wukong's actions, specifically how he ate a lot of fairy peaches and used magic to immobilize them in the garden.

sentences.text: 王母娘娘去了她的儿子玉皇大帝那里，告诉他这个事情。
sentences.translation: The Queen Mother of the West went to her son, the Jade Emperor, and told him about this matter.
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces the Queen Mother of the West (a figure in Chinese mythology) going to her son, the Jade Emperor, to inform him about something. The structure '去了' indicates the action of going has been completed, and '告诉' is used to convey the action of telling.

words.definition: The Queen Mother of the West

content.raw_text: 王母娘娘还没有说完，准备宴会的一些工人来了，告诉玉皇大帝有人吃了宴会上所有的东西、喝了所有的酒。太上老君也来见玉皇大帝，告诉他有人进了他的家，吃了他所有的金丹。最后，赤脚大仙来了，告诉玉皇大帝有人让他去了错的宴会地方！

sentences.text: 王母娘娘还没有说完，准备宴会的一些工人来了，告诉玉皇大帝有人吃了宴会上所有的东西，喝了所有的酒。
sentences.translation: Queen Mother Niangniang had not finished speaking when some workers preparing for the banquet arrived and told the Jade Emperor that someone had eaten all the food at the banquet and drank all the wine.
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes a situation where workers inform the Jade Emperor that someone has consumed all the food and wine at the banquet, interrupting Queen Mother Niangniang's speech.

sentences.text: 太上老君也来见玉皇大帝，告诉他有人进了他的家，吃了他所有的金丹。
sentences.translation: The Supreme Elder Lord also came to see the Jade Emperor, telling him that someone had entered his home and eaten all of his golden elixirs.
sentences.explanation: This sentence involves the use of past tense markers '了' and '过'. The phrase '金丹' refers to 'golden elixirs', a concept from Taoist alchemy.

sentences.text: 最后，赤脚大仙来了，告诉玉皇大帝有人让他去了错的宴会地方！
sentences.translation: Finally, the Barefoot Immortal came and told the Jade Emperor that someone had led him to the wrong banquet location!
sentences.explanation: The structure '有人让他去了' might be confusing for learners as it combines the words 'someone led him to go' in a different order than English.

content.raw_text: 这些事情对玉皇大帝来说太多了。他很生气，他叫来了很多神仙。他们中间有东西二星，南北二神，五山神仙，四江龙神，天宫众神，一共十万军队。玉皇大帝要大家去花果山抓孙悟空。

sentences.text: 这些事情对玉皇大帝来说太多了。
sentences.translation: These matters are too much for the Jade Emperor.
sentences.explanation: The structure '对...来说' is used to indicate something is for someone or something to consider. In this sentence, it means 'for the Jade Emperor'.

sentences.text: 他很生气，他叫来了很多神仙。
sentences.translation: He was very angry, and he summoned many immortals.
sentences.explanation: The structure '叫来' means 'to summon' or 'to call over'. The use of '了' indicates the completion of the action.

sentences.text: 他们中间有东西二星，南北二神，五山神仙，四江龙神，天宫众神，一共十万军队。
sentences.translation: Among them are two stars of the East, two gods of the South and North, immortal gods of the Five Mountains, dragon gods of the Four Rivers, gods of the Heavenly Palace, totaling one hundred thousand troops.
sentences.explanation: The sentence describes a group of various gods and deities, totaling one hundred thousand troops, among them are stars, gods, immortal beings, dragons, and heavenly gods.

sentences.text: 玉皇大帝要大家去花果山抓孙悟空。
sentences.translation: The Jade Emperor wants everyone to go to Flower Fruit Mountain to capture Sun Wukong.
sentences.explanation: This sentence introduces the Jade Emperor, a prominent figure in Chinese mythology, instructing everyone to capture Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, at Flower Fruit Mountain. The structure is straightforward, but the cultural references may require some background knowledge.

content.raw_text: 军队在花果山上扔下一大张网要把孙悟空包在里面。然后他们都在水帘洞外面等着。

sentences.text: 军队在花果山上扔下一大张网要把孙悟空包在里面。
sentences.translation: The army dropped a large net on Flower Fruit Mountain to trap Sun Wukong inside.
sentences.explanation: This sentence showcases the use of the particle '把' to indicate the object of the verb '包'. It also introduces the measure word '张' for flat objects like nets.

words.definition: measure word for flat objects like nets, paper, etc.
particle used to indicate the object of a verb

sentences.text: 然后他们都在水帘洞外面等着。
sentences.translation: Then they all waited outside the waterfall cave.
sentences.explanation: The structure '在...外面' means 'outside of...'. The verb '等着' means 'to wait'.
